Only my `FastDatePrinterAgentTest` exists under `src/test/java`, and 36 of 38 tests pass. The 2 remaining failures are genuine bugs in `FastDatePrinter`, not test mistakes.

## Summary

I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDatePrinterAgentTest.java` (38 tests, self-contained, JUnit 5, Java 8 syntax). 36 tests pass. Two fail, and both indicate real bugs in `FastDatePrinter`:

1. **`testConstructorNullLocaleThrowsNullPointerException`** — The constructor's javadoc states: *"@throws NullPointerException Thrown if pattern, timeZone, or locale is null."* But the constructor does `this.locale = LocaleUtils.toLocale(locale);`, and `LocaleUtils.toLocale(Locale)` silently falls back to `Locale.getDefault()` for a `null` input instead of throwing. So passing a `null` locale never throws, contradicting the documented contract.

2. **`testFormatCalendarConvertsToPrinterTimeZoneWithoutPriorMillisAccess`** — `DatePrinter.format(Calendar)` is documented so that "the TimeZone specified during construction of the Parser will determine the TimeZone used in the formatted string," regardless of the Calendar's own zone. This works correctly via `format(Calendar, StringBuffer)` (which converts through `calendar.getTime()`), but `format(Calendar)` / `format(Calendar, Appendable)` do `calendar.clone(); actual.setTimeZone(timeZone)`. If the calendar's time-in-millis was never materialized first (i.e., only `set(...)` was called, the normal way to build a `Calendar`), `Calendar.setTimeZone` on the clone causes the *existing field values* to be reinterpreted as already being in the new zone, instead of converting the instant — so the output silently keeps the original zone's wall-clock values unconverted. For a `Calendar` in `Asia/Tokyo` at `2021-01-01 05:30:00` formatted with a UTC printer, this produces `"2021-01-01 05:30:00"` instead of the correct `"2020-12-31 20:30:00"`, and disagrees with the other overload given the exact same input.
